geo_headlines: TRUMP IMPOSES 50% TARIFFS ON CERTAIN CANADIAN GOODS — Section 338 of 1930 Tariff Act (first-ever use). Wine, hockey sticks, cement, motor vehicles, dairy, alcohol. Effective Aug 19. Energy, potash, fish, critical minerals EXEMPT. USMCA-covered items HIT.

10-DAY CEASEFIRE PROPOSAL — Qatar, Pakistan, Egypt mediators floated a 10-day US-Iran truce to revive interim deal; during pause, would negotiate longer-term Hormuz passage arrangement (Reuters/Axios)
10TH CONSECUTIVE NIGHT of US strikes on Iran — operation expanded beyond southern targets (Reuters/AP/Al Jazeera); no US KIA reported overnight
IRAN STRUCK TANKER in Strait of Hormuz Sunday — Iranian footage shows 'burning tanker'; two tankers now reported damaged (AP, The National)
OIL EASED overnight on ceasefire optimism — Brent $88.79 (-0.4%), WTI $82.61 (steady), both off Monday's five-week highs
CHIP REBOUND — Big Tech earnings this week: Alphabet + Tesla + Intel + IBM report Wed; SOX rallied Mon (+0.6% at close, was +4% intraday)
MON 10Y yield +5.7bp to 4.598%; 30Y still above 5%; DXY ~101 on 3-day win streak
CANADA response: PM Carney statement — 'more than 20 new economic and security partnerships' — 30-day window before tariffs bite leaves room for negotiation
headline: Risk-on premarket on ceasefire hopes: 10-day truce proposal, chip rebound. But: Trump 50% Canada tariff hits USMCA goods Aug 19, 10th night of US strikes on Iran, tanker attacks in Hormuz. Big Tech earnings Wed is the setup.
client_frame: The overnight tape has flipped from Monday's cautious tone to constructive: ES +0.56%, NQ +1.30% on chip rebound + ceasefire hope. Qatar, Pakistan and Egypt have floated a 10-day US-Iran truce; during the pause the parties would negotiate longer-term Hormuz passage. Whether it holds is the question — the 10th consecutive night of US strikes on Iran also completed overnight, and Iran struck a tanker in Hormuz Sunday. Oil eased modestly on the ceasefire headline: Brent $88.79, WTI $82.61, both off Monday's five-week highs. The rate market didn't get the memo yet — 30Y still above 5%, DXY 101, CME September hike odds ticked to 55% (from 51% Fri). Client framing: the base case remains an oil-supply-shock plus geopolitical-risk regime layered on the AI/semi de-rating, now with two fresh wildcards. First, the 10-day ceasefire — if it holds, energy trades unwind fast and equity beta rotates back toward AI/semis. If it fails, we go higher on oil and lower on the tape. Second, the 50 percent tariffs Trump imposed on select Canadian goods yesterday — Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act, first-ever use — take effect August 19. USMCA-covered goods including autos, wine, dairy and hockey sticks are hit. Energy and critical minerals are exempt. Practical impact is smaller than the number suggests because 30 days leaves negotiating room and PM Carney's statement was measured, but Canada exposure names (autos, forest products, rail) are worth watching. Real setup this week is Big Tech earnings Wed: Alphabet, Tesla, Intel, IBM. Given SOX is still in a technical bear market off June, that print is the tape's real referendum. Position for variance, not direction.
